answer: The regulator rates each clock against the stars and writes its rate in the regulator's book, and no clock may be trusted until its rate is filed. A basalt clock set by guesswork fails the rating: at the marble of the night the hands must match the stars the book recorded, and a guessed clock loses minutes by dawn. Forging the rating means keeping a chronometer for a year, rating it 300 nights and paying 14,800, while the trellis figure in the regulator's book is read by every astronomer, so a clock whose rate was never measured is put back on the bench.
